deals.whyRanked: Allegiant's calendar still shows $56 one-way legs on both Nov 7 and Nov 14 — pairing those keeps Knoxville the cheapest verified fare of the week again, with the Smokies still 45 minutes from downtown.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown's compact grid is easy to explore alone on foot, and the Cosby and Greenbrier entrances to the Smokies are a short solo drive with none of the Cades Cove crowds.

highlights: World's Fair Park and the Sunsphere observation deck
Market Square's farmers' stalls and buskers
Ijams Nature Center's quarry swimming hole and trails
South Knoxville's urban wilderness bike/hike loop
Cosby entrance to the Great Smoky Mountains
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, ride the elevator up the Sunsphere for a skyline view, then dinner on Market Square.
Day 2 — Rent a car for the Cosby entrance: the Hen Wallow Falls trail, with a stop at Foothills Parkway overlooks on the drive back.
Day 3 — Morning loop at Ijams Nature Center, then Market Square's farmers' stalls before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown is flat and walkable end to end; a rental car is required to reach any Smokies trailhead.
guide.stayArea: Downtown near Market Square or Gay Street — walkable to restaurants and the Tennessee Theatre.

deals.whyRanked: Allegiant prices the outbound leg at $60 on Nov 14 and the return as low as $44 on Nov 12 — about $104 round trip, second-cheapest of the week, with the Everglades under an hour away.
deals.soloWhy: The free Sun Trolley links the beach and Las Olas without a car, and the lit beachfront promenade stays comfortable for a solo evening walk.

highlights: Shark Valley's flat 15-mile Everglades bike loop
Fort Lauderdale beachfront promenade
Riverwalk Arts & Entertainment District
Bonnet House Museum & Gardens
Las Olas Boulevard gallery stroll
itinerary: Day 1 — Check in near the beach, sunset walk on the promenade, dinner and people-watching on Las Olas.
Day 2 — Rent a car for the Shark Valley bike loop — alligators sunning along the canal — back in time for a Riverwalk stroll.
Day 3 — Bonnet House gardens in the morning, a water-taxi hop to Las Olas for lunch before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: The free Sun Trolley covers downtown, Las Olas, and the beach; a rental car is worth it only for the Everglades day trip.
guide.stayArea: The beachfront or Las Olas — both walkable to restaurants, the promenade, and water taxi stops.

deals.whyRanked: Southwest's calendar confirms $79 one-way legs on both Nov 18 and Nov 25 — a genuine $158 round trip, the best mid-price fare verified this week, with Enchanted Rock and Barton Springs both an easy solo day trip.
deals.soloWhy: South Congress and downtown are flat and walkable, live music venues are easy to drop into solo any night, and Barton Springs Pool is a relaxed solo swim.

highlights: Barton Springs Pool's year-round 68-degree water
South Congress Avenue murals and shops
Live music on Rainey Street and East 6th
McKinney Falls State Park's Onion Creek trail
Enchanted Rock's pink granite summit dome
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, wander South Congress, swim at Barton Springs at golden hour, catch a set on Rainey Street.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Enchanted Rock: the roughly 4-mile Summit Trail loop plus the flatter Loop Trail around the base.
Day 3 — Morning at McKinney Falls' Onion Creek trail, East 6th Street food trucks before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown, South Congress, and the Lady Bird Lake trail are walkable or a short scooter ride apart; a rental car is needed for Enchanted Rock or McKinney Falls.
guide.stayArea: South Congress (SoCo) or downtown near Rainey Street — walkable to music venues and the lake trail.
food: Franklin Barbecue (arrive early or order ahead)

deals.whyRanked: JetBlue's one-way floor has climbed to $86 for November travel now that the late-September $59 sale has expired — about $172 round trip, tied with Baltimore, but the Metro plus free Smithsonians keep DC's solo score the highest of the five.
deals.soloWhy: The Metro reaches nearly every monument and museum, the Mall is safe to walk solo well into the evening, and the Smithsonians are free.

highlights: Smithsonian museums (all free)
Tidal Basin loop past the Jefferson Memorial
Eastern Market on a weekend morning
Shenandoah's Skyline Drive
Great Falls Park overlook on the Potomac
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, drop bags, Tidal Basin loop at golden hour, dinner near Eastern Market.
Day 2 — Rent a car for Shenandoah: Skyline Drive up to the Hawksbill summit trailhead, back for an H Street dinner.
Day 3 — Great Falls Park's towpath in the morning, pick one Smithsonian before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Metro covers the Mall, museums, and most neighborhoods; a rental car is only needed for Shenandoah or Great Falls.
guide.stayArea: Near a Metro stop on the Orange/Blue/Silver line (Capitol Hill or Foggy Bottom) for the fastest reach to the Mall.

deals.whyRanked: Southwest's $59 one-way sale has expired; the floor is now $86 each way for November and December travel — about $172 round trip, tied with DC, but Assateague's 2.5-hour drive and a lower solo score keep it fifth.
deals.soloWhy: The Inner Harbor and Fells Point are flat and walkable with plenty of counter-seating for solo dining, linked by a water taxi so a car is never needed downtown.

highlights: National Aquarium
Fells Point's cobblestone waterfront
Fort McHenry National Monument
American Visionary Art Museum
Lexington Market's Faidley Seafood counter
itinerary: Day 1 — Inner Harbor on arrival, National Aquarium, water taxi to Fells Point for oysters at a counter stool.
Day 2 — Fort McHenry in the morning, Federal Hill for the skyline overlook, dinner back in Fells Point.
Day 3 — American Visionary Art Museum, Lexington Market crab cakes before an evening flight.
guide.gettingAround: Inner Harbor, Fells Point, and Fort McHenry are covered by the water taxi and a short walk or rideshare; no rental car needed unless heading to Assateague.
guide.stayArea: Fells Point or the Inner Harbor — walkable, close to the water taxi and restaurants.
